newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada February wholesale trade rises from January.
newsitem.headline: Canada February wholesale trade rises from January.

text.p: Canada's wholesale trade rose 3.0 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in February from January to C$23.09 billion, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
Sales, adj C$23.09 bln 3.0 pct 13.8 pct
Inventories, adj C$32.73 bln 1.2 pct 3.9 pct
Note - dollar figures are billions. Other figures are percentage changes.
StatsCan also revised its figure for January sales to C$22.43 billion from C$22.14 billion.

Statistics Canada said across-the-board increases led to the 3.0 percent jump in sales by wholesalers in February, making February's gain the largest jump in sales since March 1991, when the wholesaling industry started coming out of recession.

The federal agency said wholesalers of farm machinery and equipment were the most active in February, with sales increasing by 16.6 percent. Motor vehicles and parts rose 7.2 percent, and lumber and building materials increases 5.0 percent.

Wholesalers increased their inventories by 1.2 percent February, the largest monthly increase in two years, StatsCan said. The only declines in inventories were in motor vehicles and parts, falling 0.5 percent, and in lumber and building materials, also down 0.5 percent.

But increases in sales outpaced the rise in inventories, helping the inventory-to-sales ratio to fall to its lowest level since December 1994, down to 1.42 in February from 1.44 in January, the agency said.
